source: https://github.com/AnicetNgrt/hpc-sandbox-benchmarks/tree/ed8ec45a1ee0f5058ca99944d9c569d49b2f8e67/docs/results/2026-08-24-cpu (leaderboard.md, README.md, run.json), linked from boat.dev's benchmark section
measured_on: 2026-08-24 (Ascii Box, Freestyle); the other rows are from the vendor's July CI run
note: Vendor-published (boat.dev was formerly Ascii Box; its row is 'Ascii Box (bare metal)'). Despite that label, 27.67 is NOT a bare-metal host score: run.json's observedSpecs for that row report a 4 vCPU / 7.76 GiB KVM guest (virtualization kvm, manufacturer QEMU, Q35, SeaBIOS, detectedIsolation vm) with cpuModel AMD Ryzen 9 9950X, egress OVH Lille. It is a sandbox VM on a dedicated host. The host itself was not measured. boat.dev's '1,000 runs in 36 s' is 1000 / 27.67 runs/s. Their run: PTS pts/node-web-tooling-1.0.1 with DynamicRunCount, median of 21 trials on fresh machines; the Node version is not stated.

pts_rand_read_iops.note: pts/fio-2.1.0: 4KB rand read, O_DIRECT, libaio, 1 job, iodepth 64, 1 GiB, 60 s. Same job here, but a loop file on a shared runner cannot speak for NVMe

pts_rand_write_iops.note: pts/fio-2.1.0: 4KB rand write, same job. A loop file on a shared runner cannot speak for NVMe

pts_seq_write_mibps.note: pts/fio-2.1.0: 1MB seq write, same job. PTS labels this MB/s, but it equals their 1MB IOPS (5837), so it is MiB/s. A loop file on a shared runner cannot speak for NVMe

same_benchmark.source: https://openbenchmarking.org/test/pts/node-web-tooling, per-CPU runs/s averages, retrieved 2026-11-03: 'AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core' 10.3 +/- 0.4 (4 public results), 'AMD Ryzen 9 9950X 16-Core' 28.8 +/- 2.6 (30 public results)

cpu_scaling.limits: the vendor's repo has no EPYC 7763 row, so the CPU ratios come from public data with mixed Node versions, setups and sample sizes (the 7763 row has 4 results). The VM/host ratio was measured on a shared, nested Azure VM and may not transfer to a dedicated host. It says nothing about memory, disk or network hardware.
